evidence_spine.claim: Blockbuster print: units +~96% YoY (~108k), revenue +~200% YoY to ~$3.3B, FIRST-EVER positive net income (~$45M) but net margin only ~1-2%; gross-profit-per-unit at a record high. The single best quarter ever, on the thinnest of margins.

Management explicitly attributes an unusually favorable slice of profitability to a TRANSITORY pricing tailwind in the sourcing/supply market ('unlike anything in my career'); multiple analysts pressed on H2 normalization. Earnings quality is self-flagged as non-repeatable.

Leading indicator: industry WHOLESALE price index for the good is at record highs but just printed its FIRST month-over-month decline off the peak. The tailwind that made the quarter is already rolling over.

Balance sheet is fragile and funding-dependent: first-half operating cash OUTFLOW ~$(1.14)B, cash only ~$0.2B, total debt ~$3.1B and rising, ongoing capital-intensive build-out. No cushion to absorb a margin/demand normalization without external capital.

Priced-in / exhaustion signal: stock rose only ~2-3% on a blockbuster print, sitting near all-time highs after a large multi-year run; ~$60B equity value at ~7x trailing sales, P/E n/m. Great news produced almost no move -> the bull case is already in the price.

Demand tailwind is itself a transitory macro condition: a supply shortage in the NEW/primary version of the good is diverting buyers into the second-hand market; a large peer also just reported record demand. When primary supply heals, the demand pull-forward reverses at the same time the pricing tailwind fades (double whammy).

kill_criteria: Flip bullish if: (a) the wholesale price index stabilizes/re-accelerates and stays elevated for 2+ prints (tailwind durable, not transitory); OR (b) the company demonstrates record gross-profit-per-unit DURABILITY without the pricing tailwind (structural cost-out, not price mix); OR (c) it de-risks the balance sheet via large equity raise AND turns operating cash flow positive; OR (d) unit-share gains keep compounding at self-funding economics AFTER primary-good supply normalizes. Absent these, the down/priced-in thesis holds.
